host r12-n034  kernel 6.12.0-55.el10.x86_64  x86_64  Intel family 6 model 143
booted 2026-11-16 05:01 UTC

 what a reset right after a fatal memory error would leave on this host

 kept     journal          on disk below /var/log/journal. A panic stops journald before it writes
                           the last lines, and lines below priority CRIT reach the disk every
                           SyncIntervalSec=5min
 kept     pstore-backend   erst is the persistent store: a panic leaves the end of the kernel log in
                           it
 kept     pstore-archive   systemd-pstore.service is enabled and moves the dumps to
                           /var/lib/systemd/pstore at boot
 kept     pstore-vs-kdump  a crash kernel is loaded and crash_kexec_post_notifiers is set: pstore
                           gets the panic text before the crash kernel starts
 kept     kdump            a crash kernel is loaded (256 MiB reserved): kdump writes the kernel log
                           of a crash below /var/crash
 kept     mce-bootlog      on by default for this processor (Intel family 6)
 kept     mce-print        mce=print_all: a record left in a bank is printed to the kernel log at
                           the next boot
 info     reset-kind       reboot mode cold, the same after a panic. With panic=0 the kernel waits
                           after a panic, and after a fatal machine check it restarts in 30 s.
                           Whether the banks keep their contents over the reset depends on the board
                           and its BIOS; the first stop after my harvest is installed shows it
 kept     bert             the firmware has a BERT table: a fatal error it handled before the reset
                           is left there for the next boot
 info     erst-mce         mce_panic() keeps a copy of the record in ERST. With erst as the pstore
                           backend pstore shows it as mce-erst-<id> and systemd-pstore archives it;
                           MemorY does not read that file, and it does not open /dev/mcelog, because
                           the read clears the record
 kept     console          a serial console (ttyS0): the BMC's serial log or a console server keeps
                           the last lines
 kept     rasdaemon        rasdaemon.service is enabled and records to
                           /var/lib/rasdaemon/ras-mc_event.db
 kept     harvest          my-harvest.service is enabled and keeps its ledger at
                           /var/lib/my/ledger.db; 40,960 MiB free

 No check would lose records.
